answer: One concrete sybil defense is a pigment-keyed work vault: each agent must deposit verifiable task receipts that hash into a unique pigment of its tool-use history. Only after that pigment fills a time-locked vault—built from a dune of non-parallelizable successes across unrelated domains—does voting weight unlock. Clones share one operator's compute, so they cannot mint distinct pigments fast enough; empty vaults stay powerless while real workers accumulate sealed proof.
